attributes.body:
When learning じゃない and ではない, we briefly mentioned that these constructions are regularly partnered with the particle か, in order to form a (usually casual) question. In this lesson, we will further explore this usage.

Unlike じゃない and ではない (which need to come after a noun or な-Adjective), じゃないか is able to be attached to the end of almost any phrase, to indicate a question. This is very similar to finishing a sentence with 'isn't it?' in English.

When じゃないか is too casual, ではないか will be used instead. Despite being more formal, this may sound a bit stiff at times, so is best only used when politeness is expected.

attributes.description: じゃない & じゃん NOT ONLY NEGATION!

attributes.body: かもしれない and じゃないか can both appear at the end of a sentence, but differ in nuance. かもしれない expresses uncertainty, e.g. おいしいかもしれない ('It might be tasty.'). じゃないか is more emphatic and seeks agreement, e.g. おいしいじゃないか ('It's tasty, isn't it?' or 'I'm telling you it's tasty, don't you agree?').

でしょう, in addition to expressing conjecture, can also seek confirmation or agreement from the listener (e.g., 面白いでしょう = 'Interesting, right?'). じゃないか is more forceful and casual, implying the speaker strongly believes something and expects the listener to agree (e.g., 面白いじゃないか = 'Interesting, isn't it!'). Note that でしょう is polite, while じゃないか is very casual.

Both じゃないか and のではないだろうか are negative questions similar to the English '...isn't it?' but differ in nuance. じゃないか is used to confirm something the speaker believes to be true, often with a confrontational or challenging tone, e.g. 'It's (A), isn't it!?' In contrast, のではないだろうか is more tentative, expressing uncertainty and seeking confirmation, e.g. 'Do you suppose it's (A)?'.

second_relatable.title: のではないだろうか
second_relatable.meaning: I think ... isn't it?, It might be that..., Don't you agree?

attributes.body: じゃない follows a noun or な-Adjective to express 'is not' or 'are not.' じゃないか, with the addition of か, changes the meaning to 'Isn't it...?' as in 本じゃない ('It isn't a book') vs. 本じゃないか ('It's a book, isn't it?') While じゃない is used only after nouns or な-Adjectives, じゃないか can follow い-Adjectives and verbs as well.

Both ～のだろうか and じゃないか seek confirmation, but with different levels of confidence. のだろうか expresses uncertainty, used for low-confidence guesses or suppositions, e.g. 'I wonder if (A)?'. In contrast, じゃないか is used to confirm something the speaker believes to be true, often with a confrontational or challenging tone, e.g. 'It's (A), isn't it!?'.

じゃないか and ね both seek agreement at the end of a sentence, but they have different nuances and levels of politeness. じゃないか is casual and assertive, often strongly insisting on an opinion, and can feel confrontational, making it best suited for use among close friends. In contrast, ね is softer and used widely to seek gentle agreement or confirmation in various contexts.

だろう, in addition to expressing conjecture ('It's probably…'), can seek confirmation or agreement from the listener (e.g., 面白いだろう = 'It's interesting, right?'). じゃないか is more forceful and assertive, suggesting the speaker strongly believes something and expects agreement (e.g., 面白いじゃないか = 'It's interesting, isn't it!'). Both are casual forms and should be avoided in polite conversation.
